updates.name: Bethany Muñoz Delgado
updates.bio: Natural Resource Specialist with NRCS's Central National Technology Support Center (USDA) and NRCS co-lead for the Northern Forests Climate Hub, where she helps develop and share climate science for NRCS programs and other audiences. She trained in geography at Texas A&M and in forest resources at Oregon State and the University of Maine (PhD).
updates.research_interests: forest ecology and management; geospatial data management and analysis

updates.name: Peter O'Brien
updates.bio: Research Agronomist with the National Laboratory for Agriculture and the Environment (USDA ARS) in Ames, Iowa, and ARS co-lead for the Northern Forests Climate Hub, supporting climate-informed agroforestry and soil health work. His research asks how cover crops, alternative rotations and agroforestry change the way farm systems capture, store and use water. He holds NDSU graduate degrees.
updates.research_interests: soil water dynamics; agronomy; agroforestry; cover crops and diversified crop rotations

updates.name: Stephen Handler
updates.bio: Listed as Deputy Director on the Climate Change Response Framework team, which NIACS and the USDA Northern Forests Climate Hub coordinate jointly, and coordinator of the Northwoods Framework for Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan. He works with partners on vulnerability assessments, adaptation planning and education, and considers how adaptation applies to wildlife, logging and Indigenous land management. Joined NIACS in 2011.
updates.research_interests: climate change vulnerability assessment; forest climate adaptation planning; adaptation for wildlife management and logging practices; Indigenous perspectives on land management; forest carbon assessment

updates.name: Cory Owens
updates.bio: Assistant State Conservationist for Partnerships with USDA NRCS in Oregon and NRCS co-lead of the USDA Northwest Climate Hub, working with local, state and national partners to pool conservation resources. Her background is soil science (Oregon State; MS from UC Davis through the Peace Corps Master's International Program), including graduate work on indigenous soil knowledge in Senegal.

updates.name: Edward G. Stets
updates.bio: Research Ecologist in the USGS Water Mission Area, based in Mounds View, Minnesota, studying water quality and environmental change mainly in freshwater systems. He brings biogeochemistry, statistics, trend analysis and project management to national NAWQA and IWP projects and regional work in the Upper Mississippi. He earned a PhD in ecology from the University of Minnesota (2007).
updates.research_interests: surface water quality; water budgets; land use change and human impacts on water; nonpoint-source pollution; freshwater ecosystems; isotopic and statistical analysis
updates.current_affiliation: U.S. Geological Survey, Water Resources Mission Area
